panels.title: Nothing is unpacked on a server

params.text:
The package you are reading is a .h5p file, which is a zip archive. It sits on a plain file host and is read in place: the player fetches the archive’s index from its tail with one Range request, and then asks for exactly the bytes each file needs.

There is no server-side code, no extraction step, and nothing to install on the host beyond static files.

metadata.title: Nothing is unpacked on a server

panels.title: A Service Worker is the file server

params.text:
The H5P runtime expects to load scripts, styles and media from URLs. A Service Worker answers those URLs from the archive, so to the runtime this looks like an ordinary H5P site.

The worker keeps no state of its own. A browser may stop it between two requests, and it rebuilds what it needs from a small record in IndexedDB each time.

metadata.title: A Service Worker is the file server

panels.title: Long work runs beside the page

params.text:
Downloading an archive from a host that ignores Range, or inflating a large compressed video, can take minutes. A Service Worker is not allowed to run that long, so a second worker owned by the page does it and hands the result over in 8 MB pieces through the browser’s Cache API.

While that download is still running, the player already indexes the archive from the local headers as they arrive, and starts the content as soon as its libraries are in.

metadata.title: Long work runs beside the page

panels.title: Video starts before it has arrived

params.text:
A video that is stored in the zip is served with Range requests straight out of the archive, so it plays and seeks at once. One that is compressed has to be inflated from the front; the player serves the prefix that exists and lets the rest follow.

The one case nothing can shorten is a compressed mp4 whose index sits at its end. The repository ships a script that rewrites such a package once, storing the media and moving the index to the front.

metadata.title: Video starts before it has arrived

params.text: Any zip can be handed to this player, so entry names that try to escape the package root are rejected rather than repaired, every file is served with the right Content-Type, and the frame the content runs in carries a Content Security Policy that names the few origins real content types reach.
